questions.question: The November 2018 mapwork paper was set on which map extract?
options: The 1:50 000 topographic map of Pietermaritzburg with a 1:10 000 orthophoto extract
A satellite image of the Karoo

questions.question: On the current papers, the thirty mapwork marks of Section B are split as:
options: Fifteen for GIS and fifteen for calculations
Ten for map skills and calculations, twelve for map interpretation, eight for GIS
Twenty for theory and ten for drawing

questions.question: Standing information worth reading in the map margin before any question includes:
options: The sheet index, scale, contour interval and magnetic declination note

subtopics.title: Question 1 — Fifteen Multiple-Choice Marks on the Maps

questions.question: A ring of closed contours with heights rising toward the centre represents:
A true bearing of 120 degrees from a point places the target roughly:
South African 1:50 000 sheet codes like the Pietermaritzburg 2930 family are built from:
options: The latitude and longitude of the degree square, plus letters locating a sixteenth of it
The population of the main town

subtopics.title: Question 2.1 — Map Codes, Grid References and the Hiking Trail

questions.question: A complete coordinate answer for Town Hill at N must include:
options: Degrees, minutes and seconds with the hemisphere letters south and east

questions.question: The hiking trail in block F6 follows a long finger of high ground projecting between valleys. This feature is a:
An alphanumeric reference like F6 differs from a coordinate because it:
options: Is more precise than a coordinate
Locates a block on the map rather than fixing an exact point

subtopics.title: Question 2.2 — The Average Gradient Calculation, Marked Like the Memo

questions.question: In the 2018 gradient question, the vertical interval of 237,9 metres came from:
options: The contour interval of the map
1 057,9 metres at the trigonometrical station minus the 820-metre contour at O

questions.question: The measured 3,9 centimetres became a horizontal equivalent of 1 950 metres because:
options: At 1:50 000, each centimetre on the map represents 500 metres in reality
The memo required doubling the measurement

questions.question: The memo accepted final answers from 1:7,9 to 1:8,4 because:
options: The examiners disagreed about the formula
Gradient answers never need to be exact
Rulers differ by a millimetre, so a measurement range of 3,8 to 4 centimetres was allowed

questions.question: A candidate who wrote only '1:8,2' with no working risked:
options: Earning only the answer mark and gambling the stepwise method marks
Being penalised for using a ratio

questions.question: Vertical exaggeration is calculated as:
options: Vertical interval divided by horizontal equivalent
Vertical scale divided by horizontal scale, with the answer stated in times

questions.question: With a vertical scale of 1:10 000 and a horizontal scale of 1:50 000, the vertical exaggeration is:
Cross-sections use vertical exaggeration because:
options: Drawn to true scale, the relief would be almost invisible on paper
It changes the real steepness of the land

subtopics.title: Question 3 — Frost, Aspect and Streams: Theory Applied to the Map

questions.question: Farmers at the low-lying point M fear clear, calm winter nights because:
options: Katabatic drainage ponds cold air on the valley floor, forming an inversion and a frost pocket
The river floods on clear nights
The urban heat island reaches the farm

questions.question: In the Southern Hemisphere, the residential slope that is warmer and historically more desirable is the one oriented toward the:
options: North, which receives more direct midday sun

questions.question: Two first-order streams join, and their stream is later joined by another first-order stream. The order below that second junction is:
options: Second order, because only two streams of equal order raise the order

questions.question: The height 1 057,9 metres attached to the trigonometrical station is an example of:
options: Attribute data describing a located feature

questions.question: Scale is relevant to a geographical query because:
options: A street-level question needs large-scale data like the 1:10 000 orthophoto; detail invisible at small scale cannot be queried
All queries use the same scale
Larger scales always cover larger areas

questions.question: To identify housing at flood risk along the Msunduzi River, a GIS analyst would:
options: Buffer the river by a stated width and overlay the residential layer
Convert all data to attribute tables
